disclaimer: Regulatory intelligence, not legal advice. All wording is potential-gap language, never a confirmed breach or liability determination.

_meta.authoring_coverage: Clause libraries, wording templates, priority model and framework catalog are complete. findings[] fully authors the scanner-backed finding types across all four countries, plus representative proposed stubs. The complete 85-code catalogue is in the companion Markdown (Table A) and summarised in catalogue_index below; proposed codes are to be authored in the next pass using the identical mapping schema.

priority_model.penalty_rule: Penalties are indicative maximums depending on circumstances, never presented as guaranteed financial loss.

wording_templates.potential_compliance_gap: This finding may indicate a gap against {clause_reference} ({law_name}). A compliance review is recommended to confirm applicability.
wording_templates.possible_notification_obligation: If personal information was actually exposed, this may give rise to a notification obligation under {law_name}. Whether it does depends on the facts - seek advice before notifying.
wording_templates.governance_concern: This reflects a governance gap: {gap}. Technical fixes alone may not prevent recurrence.
wording_templates.director_oversight_concern: Cyber-risk oversight may be relevant to director/officer duties under {clause_reference}, depending on the organisation's circumstances.
wording_templates.sector_specific_applicability: {clause_reference} applies only if the organisation is {condition}.
wording_templates.guidance_only_mapping: {framework} is guidance/standard, not law. It is provided to help prioritise remediation.
wording_templates.legal_review_recommendation: This is regulatory intelligence, not legal advice. Legal or compliance review may be required before relying on it.
wording_templates.forthcoming_law: {law_name} is enacted but not yet in force; treat this as a forward-looking consideration, not a current obligation.

iso_27001_2022.note: Annex A themes A.5-A.8. Use 2022 numbering.

pci_dss_4_0_1.applicability: only if cardholder data is processed

framework_catalog.legacy_note: ISO/IEC 27001:2013 numbering (e.g. A.9.4, A.12.6) is superseded. Map A.9.4 -> A.5.15/A.8.5 and A.12.6 -> A.8.8.

AU.name: Australia
AU.notes: Privacy Act has a small-business exemption below A$3M turnover (with exceptions). Sector laws (SOCI, CPS 234) and ransomware-payment reporting apply only to covered entities.

AU-PRIV-APP11.plain_english_summary: An APP entity must take reasonable steps to protect personal information from misuse, interference, loss and unauthorised access, modification or disclosure (11.1), and destroy or de-identify it when no longer needed (11.2).
AU-PRIV-APP11.why_relevant: Technical security weaknesses may indicate the reasonable-steps standard is not met.
applicability_conditions: APP entity: turnover>A$3M OR health provider OR trades in personal information OR credit provider OR Cth contractor

AU-PRIV-NDB.plain_english_summary: Assess a suspected eligible data breach expeditiously (within 30 days) and, if it is likely to result in serious harm, notify the OAIC and affected individuals as soon as practicable.
AU-PRIV-NDB.why_relevant: Applies where personal information is actually exposed, not to a control weakness alone.
AU-PRIV-NDB.source: OAIC Data Breach Preparation and Response guide

AU-PRIV-PENALTY.clause_title: Serious or repeated interference with privacy
AU-PRIV-PENALTY.plain_english_summary: Civil penalty for serious or repeated interference with privacy, up to the greater of A$50M, three times the benefit, or 30% of adjusted turnover.
AU-PRIV-PENALTY.why_relevant: Indicative maximum enforcement context; court-imposed on OAIC application, not automatic.
AU-PRIV-PENALTY.source: Privacy Legislation Amendment (Enforcement and Other Measures) Act 2022

AU-CORP-180.clause_title: Care and diligence - directors' and officers' duties
AU-CORP-180.plain_english_summary: Directors and officers must exercise their powers and duties with the care and diligence a reasonable person would exercise; cyber-risk management can fall within this duty.
AU-CORP-180.why_relevant: Poor cyber governance may be relevant to director duties (cf. ASIC v RI Advice Group).
AU-CORP-180.source: Corporations Act 2001 s180; ASIC v RI Advice Group [2022] FCA 496

AU-CYBER-RANSOM.plain_english_summary: Covered entities must report a ransomware payment within 72 hours of making it or becoming aware it has been made.
AU-CYBER-RANSOM.why_relevant: Relevant to ransomware-entry findings for covered entities only.

AU-SOCI.plain_english_summary: Responsible entities for critical infrastructure assets must maintain a risk-management program and report incidents.

AU-CPS234.plain_english_summary: APRA-regulated entities must maintain information-security capability commensurate with threats.

AU-ACL.plain_english_summary: Businesses must not make misleading representations about their security.
AU-ACL.why_relevant: Relevant where public security claims are made and not met.

AU-E8.plain_english_summary: ACSC-recommended baseline mitigations (patching, MFA, restrict admin, backups, etc.).

NZ.name: New Zealand
NZ.notes: No small-business exemption. There is no fixed 72-hour notification deadline in the Privacy Act 2020; the standard is 'as soon as practicable' where serious harm is likely.

NZ-PRIV-IPP5.clause_title: Storage and security of personal information
NZ-PRIV-IPP5.plain_english_summary: An agency holding personal information must protect it with security safeguards that are reasonable in the circumstances.
NZ-PRIV-IPP5.why_relevant: Technical security weaknesses may indicate reasonable safeguards are not in place.

NZ-PRIV-NOTIF.plain_english_summary: Where a privacy breach has caused or is likely to cause serious harm, notify the Privacy Commissioner and affected individuals as soon as practicable after becoming aware of it.
NZ-PRIV-NOTIF.why_relevant: Applies to actual breaches likely to cause serious harm. No fixed 72-hour rule.

NZ-CO-137.clause_title: Director's duty of care; duty to act in good faith
NZ-CO-137.plain_english_summary: Directors must exercise care, diligence and skill, and act in good faith and the best interests of the company.
NZ-CO-137.why_relevant: Cyber-risk oversight may be relevant to director duties.

NZ-FMC.plain_english_summary: Conduct and disclosure obligations for financial-markets participants.
NZ-FMC.why_relevant: Only for FMC reporting entities / licensed providers.

NZ-NCSC.plain_english_summary: Baseline cyber-security controls; NZISM applies to government/public sector.

AE.name: United Arab Emirates
AE.notes: Canonical code is AE (not 'UAE'). Federal PDPL applies onshore; its Executive Regulations were pending, so enforceability of specific obligations is to_verify. DIFC and ADGM laws apply ONLY to entities registered in those free zones.

AE-PDPL-SEC.plain_english_summary: Controllers and processors must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to secure personal data.
AE-PDPL-SEC.why_relevant: Technical weaknesses may indicate a gap against PDPL security obligations.

AE-PDPL-BREACH.plain_english_summary: Notify the UAE Data Office and, where required, affected data subjects of a personal-data breach.
AE-PDPL-BREACH.why_relevant: Applies to actual breaches; mechanics depend on the Executive Regulations.

AE-DIFC-DP.law_name: DIFC Data Protection Law No. 5 of 2020
AE-DIFC-DP.plain_english_summary: Security and breach-notification obligations for DIFC entities.

AE-ADGM-DP.plain_english_summary: Security and breach-notification obligations for ADGM entities.

AE-IA.law_name: UAE Information Assurance Regulation (TDRA); Dubai ISR
AE-IA.plain_english_summary: Information-assurance control requirements for government and critical information infrastructure.

IN.name: India
IN.notes: The currently in-force security obligations are the IT Act 2000 s43A + SPDI Rules 2011 and the CERT-In Directions 2022 (6-hour reporting). The DPDP Act 2023 is enacted but NOT yet in force pending notified Rules - present it as forthcoming, not an active obligation.

IN-ITA-43A.clause_title: Reasonable security practices for sensitive personal data
IN-ITA-43A.plain_english_summary: A body corporate handling sensitive personal data must implement reasonable security practices (ISO/IEC 27001 recognised) and may be liable to compensate for negligence.
IN-ITA-43A.why_relevant: Currently the operative security obligation in India.

IN-CERTIN.plain_english_summary: Specified cyber incidents must be reported to CERT-In within six hours of noticing; logs retained 180 days.
IN-CERTIN.why_relevant: Binding and in force; relevant to actual incidents.

IN-DPDP-8.clause_title: Reasonable security safeguards; breach notification; penalties
IN-DPDP-8.plain_english_summary: Data Fiduciaries must take reasonable security safeguards and notify breaches; penalties up to Rs 250 crore.
IN-DPDP-8.why_relevant: Forward-looking - enacted but not yet in force pending Rules.

IN-SECTOR.plain_english_summary: Cyber-security frameworks for regulated banks/NBFCs, market intermediaries and insurers.

AU.technical_description: No DMARC TXT record published for the domain.
AU.technical_risk: Receivers cannot verify From-domain alignment, enabling domain spoofing, BEC and phishing.
AU.governance_impact: No email-security/anti-impersonation policy or control in place.
AU.director_or_management_context: Email-fraud exposure may be relevant to director oversight duties depending on circumstances.
AU.regulatory_relevance: Weak email authentication may indicate 'reasonable steps' under APP 11 are not met (for APP entities).
AU.penalty_context: Indicative only; serious/repeated interference maximum under AU-PRIV-PENALTY. Not a guaranteed loss.
AU.recommended_remediation: Publish SPF and DKIM, then a DMARC record starting p=none for monitoring and progress to p=quarantine/reject.
AU.legal_wording: This finding may indicate a gap against APP 11 (Privacy Act 1988). A compliance review is recommended to confirm applicability. Regulatory intelligence, not legal advice.
AU.review_owner: Global Cyber Assurance - Compliance (pending external legal review)
